claims.text: Pre-alloyed Group IV-V powder should be used for LPBF to avoid elemental segregation.
LPBF at approximately 160-200 J/mm³ with layer rotation can produce a nearly fully dense Group IV-V RHEA.
HIP following LPBF will eliminate residual porosity.
An effective HIP treatment is 1100-1200°C at 100 MPa for 2-4 hours.
A stepwise treatment involving approximately 900°C followed by aging at 650°C for 20 hours can induce coherent precipitates.
LPBF should be conducted in high-purity argon containing less than 10 ppm oxygen.
Keeping oxygen and nitrogen below 100 ppm prevents brittle oxide or nitride formation.
The optimal microstructure contains a nanocrystalline BCC matrix.
Controlled oxygen or nitrogen can form coherent ordered interstitial complexes within the BCC matrix.
Minor Ti or Zr alloying can produce coherent BCC/B2 precipitates in the proposed Group IV-V alloys.
Coherent precipitates provide order hardening and lattice-misfit strengthening without becoming premature crack-initiation sites.
Closing pores by HIP removes stress concentrators and thereby mitigates brittle failure.
Pre-alloyed powder prevents the V and W segregation associated with mixed-elemental-powder LPBF.
Ordered interstitial complexes strengthen the alloy through Snoek-type relaxation without sacrificing ductility.
Stepwise coherent precipitation can produce simultaneous ultrahigh strength and substantial tensile ductility in a refractory alloy.
The proposed alloy will have room-temperature compressive yield strength above 1.5 GPa and tensile ductility above 10%.
The alloy will retain more than 60% of its yield strength at 800°C.
The final microstructure will contain 10-20 nm coherent precipitates and less than 0.1% porosity.
Mixed-powder LPBF WTaMoNbV samples typically achieve approximately 95% density.
The strategy may fail above 0.5 at.% interstitial content or when slow aging cooling produces incoherent brittle phases.

contradictions.description: The proposed strategy requires pre-alloyed powder, but the falsification experiment deliberately uses mixed elemental powder. Failure in that experiment would not decisively falsify the claimed benefit of the pre-alloyed-powder route.
